report:
Reviewed the complete canonical_boundary claim, three ordinary implementation entries (canonicalize_solver_goal in canonical.rs, apply_query_response in boundary.rs, apply_normalization_relation in infer_ctx.rs), three ordinary annotated tests, and the explicit TODO matrix. Requirements are joint environment/goal canonicalization; rigid/flexible roles; relative universes; substitution, residual, and output transport preserving sharing and binder scopes; atomic import; and relating a normalization result only after import.

Canonicalizer folds assumptions before the goal with shared free/inference parameter maps; nested Exists scopes save/restore binder mappings and consume fresh indices. Relative universes use a minimum absolute base and caller mappings restore identities. instantiate_query registers rigid placeholders and creates flexible variables with their domain and original universe. ResponseExtractor uses shared maps across substitutions, output, and residuals, preserves scoped binders, and asserts no raw proof inference variables escape. apply_query_response validates keys/binders, creates response-local variables once, uses one copier for all returned components, applies substitutions in an isolated child, then commits all or discards on failure. Checked universe addition rejects overflow. Captured egraph lifecycle and unifier source show commit transfers ceilings and flexible equality takes the minimum ceiling. infer_ctx canonicalize_obligation_goal excludes the expected type from Normalize input; apply_normalization_relation imports the response before relating output to expected, within an outer transaction that discards ambiguity or mismatch.

Review discovered and reproduced lost universe lowering: canonical_response_preserves_lowered_input_universe originally failed with caller Universe(2), expected Universe(1), using cargo test -p sage-test-harness canonical_response_preserves_lowered_input_universe --lib. The canonical base is 1, input relative universe 1, and proof lowers it to relative 0. Previously unchanged domain permitted input-alpha reuse and omitted the lowering from the response. The coordinated correction stores original universe in InputInstance and permits class_inputs reuse only when both domain and universe remain unchanged. Otherwise extraction emits a response-local variable and substitution; import/unification carries its lowered ceiling back. The regression now passes without weakening its assertion.

canonical_equality_round_trips_transactionally asserts a successful flexible equality response resolves the original caller input to i32. response_local_type_output_round_trips_with_sharing asserts one response binder, a caller-local tuple output, trivial residual, identical repeated witness indices, and the expected universe. The new regression asserts the previously lost pure ceiling change reaches the caller. Their fixture helpers are captured and only construct source/root/trait inputs; meaningful assertions are in the test bodies.

The existing TODO inference_canonical_boundary remains a real deferral, not test success: completing the comprehensive matrix requires combined rigid/flexible environment scenarios, nested binder capture cases, nontrivial residual sharing, wider lowering cases, and incompatible expected types with ambiguous normalization candidates. Its prerequisite is constructing and asserting that broader scenario matrix. Existing narrow tests establish substitution/output sharing and one lowering regression but do not complete that matrix. No N/A or deferred implementation entry is present. Source inspection covers the stated implementation paths; acceptance retains the explicit test deferral.

Executed cargo fmt, cargo build (passed with existing warnings), cargo test -p sage-test-harness canonical --lib (7 passed), and cargo test -p sage-test-harness round_trips --lib (4 passed) after the fix. These runs include the new regression and both substantive existing associated tests. Centralized post-codegen and Sage sanity review is assigned to the coordinator; this report records the anchor assessment only.
